newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES EASIER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES EASIER.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market shed a few points in early Tuesday's quiet, liquid market, dealers said.
"It's a fairly quiet market at the moment. Not much is happening," commented one dealer.

Discount houses were buying treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at a stable 22.64 percent but were selling them on the open market at a firmer 22.50 percent from 22.35 percent the previous day.
NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought softer at 23.5 percent from Monday's 24 percent but were selling in a stable 22.50 to 22.75 percentage range.
Bankers acceptances were buying and selling at 23 and 22.25 percent respectively, down from 23.5 and 22.35, while call money fluctuated between 21 and 22 percent from 22 percent.
Reserve Bank figures indicated a surplus of Z$84 million in the market at the start of business, down from Z$206 million on Monday.
